definition: The principle that, among models achieving similar performance, the simpler one should generally be preferred, as it is more likely to generalize well.
details: Occam's Razor informs regularization techniques and model-selection practices in machine learning, reflecting the intuition that simpler explanations are less likely to merely be fitting noise in the training data.
story: Imagine explaining a hard concept to a friend using nothing but a napkin and a pen. Think of it this way: The principle that, among models achieving similar performance, the simpler one should generally be preferred, as it is more likely to generalize well. And here is the clever part: Occam's Razor informs regularization techniques and model-selection practices in machine learning, reflecting the intuition that simpler explanations are less likely to merely be fitting noise in the training data. A small mental model that makes a big tangle suddenly simple. That is Occam's Razor (in ML) — a small key that opens a big door.
